heading: Monday, September 22, 2025
topLine: AlphaEvolve finds structures that sharpen hardness-of-approximation bounds. Also: 2 model releases: Alibaba Qwen3-Omni and DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus.

items.headline: AlphaEvolve finds structures that sharpen hardness-of-approximation bounds
items.summary: Ansh Nagda, Prabhakar Raghavan and Abhradeep Thakurta used AlphaEvolve to search for combinatorial structures in complexity theory. It found near-extremal Ramanujan graphs on up to 163 vertices; these give conditional lower bounds for certifying MAX-CUT and MAX-Independent Set on random 3- and 4-regular graphs. It also found new gadget reductions showing that MAX-4-CUT is NP-hard to approximate within 0.987 (previous best 0.9883) and MAX-3-CUT within 0.9649. AlphaEvolve found the constructions and also evolved faster verification code; the humans supplied the analytical arguments. The arXiv preprint has been revised several times and has not been peer-reviewed.

items.headline: Alibaba releases Qwen3-Omni multimodal model
items.summary: Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B is an Apache-2.0 open-weight end-to-end omni-modal model that takes text, image, audio and video input and streams text and speech output. Qwen reports state-of-the-art results on 22 of 36 audio/video benchmarks.

items.headline: DeepSeek releases DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus
items.summary: DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus is an update to V3.1 that improves language consistency (fewer mixed Chinese/English outputs) and upgrades the code and search agents. It is available in the app, web and API, with open weights on Hugging Face.
